questions.question: Critically examine the assertion that the single most effective strategy is the cultivation of individual traits like initiative and self-motivation . / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Critically examine the assertion that the single most effective strategy is the cultivation of
  • individual traits like initiative and self-motivation
  • a. Empowers personal agency – Initiative and self-motivation enable individuals to take
  • ownership of actions without external prompting.
  • b. Drives sustained behavior – Intrinsic motivation is more long-lasting than external
  • rewards
  • c. Enhances adaptability – Self-motivated individuals respond creatively to challenges
  • and uncertainty.
  • d. Supports leadership and innovation – Initiative encourages problem-solving and
  • proactive contribution in community and workplace settings.
  • e. However, individual traits alone are insufficient – Structural barriers (poverty,
  • discrimination, lack of resources) limit the ability to act even for highly motivated
  • individuals.
  • f. Social environment shapes motivation – Family, culture, institutions, and role
  • models influence the development of initiative.
  • g. Collective capacities matter – Community networks, supportive policies, and
  • enabling environments amplify individual traits.
  • h. Risk of victim-blaming – Overemphasis on personal traits may ignore systemic
  • injustices and shift responsibility onto individuals.
  • i. Balanced approach is needed – Effective strategies combine individual
  • empowerment with systemic support (education, opportunities, and social protection).j.

  • [CO2,
  • CO3]

questions.question: Analyze the causes and consequences of the culture of silence and evaluate its impact as the most pervasive societal barrier. / [CO2, CO4, CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyze the causes and consequences of the culture of silence and evaluate its impact as
  • the most pervasive societal barrier
  • a. Fear of authority and repression – People remain silent due to fear of punishment,
  • stigma, or social backlash.
  • b. Lack of political empowerment – Limited civic education and participation create
  • passive citizenship.
  • c. Internalized oppression – Marginalized groups begin to believe they have no right or
  • ability to speak.
  • d. Social norms discouraging dissent – Cultural expectations of obedience, hierarchy,
  • and respect for elders/authority suppress voice.
  • e. Consequences: perpetuation of inequality – Silence allows exploitation, corruption,
  • and injustice to continue unchallenged.
  • f. Weak democratic participation – Low levels of public discussion weaken policy
  • accountability and governance.
  • g. Stagnation of social change – Innovation and reform slow down when people do not
  • question harmful traditions or systems.
  • h. Psychological impacts – Learned helplessness, low self-confidence, and reduced
  • agency become widespread.
  • i. Impact as a societal barrier – Culture of silence becomes embedded across
  • institutions, making collective problem-solving difficult.
  • j. Breaking silence is transformational – Empowerment education, community
  • mobilization, and participatory platforms can shift societies toward justice and
  • awareness.
  • [E] /
  • [CO2,
  • CO4,
  • CO5]
